subject: Request: HelioHealth onboarding ramp amendment & downsell protections
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: HelioHealth onboarding ramp amendment & downsell protections

Team —

Quick ask: HelioHealth (large health-tech prospect) is pushing for two non-standard concessions in their 12-month SOW: 1) an opt-out clause during the onboarding ramp that lets them step down minimum committed throughput to a reduced baseline for months 3–6 if adoption lags, and 2) a downsell protection allowing them to reduce committed spend mid-term with a limited downgrade path.

They've signaled procurement will walk if we don’t permit some opt-out language. I think we can make this work with guardrails but need deal desk + exec signoff on the exact language and any required financial protections (credits, notice windows, re-onboarding fees).

Proposed guardrails (high level):
- Opt-out window: customer can elect a single ramp opt-out between day 60–90; reduction capped at 40% of committed throughput for no more than 90 days.
- Re-onboarding: 30-day notice to return to baseline; re-onboarding fee equal to 10% of one month committed spend to cover capacity churn.
- Downsell limit: overall committed MRR cannot fall below 65% of initial commit without executive approval. Any deeper downsell triggers termination/exit language.
- Price protection: during opt-out period we retain token-based billing at agreed unit rates; discounts not increased.

Attachments: HelioHealth_SOW_redline_v2.pdf (redline of SOW), deal_summary_helio.xlsx (numbers).

Requesting: a) deal desk + legal to review and sign off on amendment language, b) Vivek for executive approval of downsell cap and re-onboarding fee.

I can hop on a 20-min sync if helpful — available 11–12pm PT today.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0198

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: HelioHealth onboarding ramp amendment & downsell protections

Thanks Aisha — good summary. I reviewed the redline and have a few operational concerns that need to be surfaced before exec signoff:

1) Capacity scheduling: the proposed 40% reduction window could impact our reserved GPU pool planning if other customers spike. We should require a 72-hour advance notice to trigger the opt-out reduction and a maximum of one trigger per contract year.

2) Billing and credits: prefer a pro-rata billing approach during the opt-out rather than true credits. If we do credits, cap cumulative credits at 1 month of committed spend across the contract term.

3) SLA & fallback: need explicit fallback to a compatible, lower-cost model variant when the customer is in opt-out mode to protect unit economics.

4) Downsell approval: suggest wording that requires VP-level approval for any downsell below 70% of committed MRR — leaves some headroom for exec discretion.

I've added inline comments in the attached proposed_amendment_20270914.docx and flagged the clauses that need legal review. If legal is OK with the re-onboarding fee as-is, I'm comfortable escalating to Vivek for the one-time exception.

Karthik
Sr. Manager, Deal Desk

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@heliohealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@heliohealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: HelioHealth onboarding ramp amendment & downsell protections

Appreciate the quick review, Karthik — answers inline below and clarifications for Vivek: 

- 72-hour notice for opt-out trigger: Helio says 48 hours is ideal but accepts 72 hours as reasonable. We should include the 72-hour requirement in the amendment.
- One trigger per contract year: Helio intends this to be a one-time safety valve; they will accept that limitation.
- Billing during opt-out: Helio wants credit back to reflect lower usage; they might push on the cap. My ask: allow pro-rata billing by default, but permit a capped credit (max 1 month) if procurement insists — requires exec approval.
- Fallback model variant: Helio is fine with moving to a smaller model profile during opt-out if needed. They asked that latency targets be preserved as much as possible.

Procurement has pushed for a 60% floor (i.e., allow downsell to 60% of committed). Karthik recommends 70% floor. Vivek — need your call here: 60% allowed with a 15% discount clawback? Or keep 70% without clawbacks?

DocuSign: Jordan sent a conditional DocuSign route pending this language — link below. If we can sign the amendment language today, we keep momentum.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/hellosign/HL-2027-042
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/HL-2027-042

My recommendation: approve opt-out with 72-hour notice, single trigger, pro-rata billing by default, capped credit (1 month) only with exec approval, and set downsell floor at 65% with Legal review on clawback mechanics.

Happy to join a quick call to walk through numbers.

—Aisha
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: HelioHealth onboarding ramp amendment & downsell protections

Thanks for the clear framing. I approve escalated terms with the following executive conditions:

1) Downsizing floor: approve 65% floor of committed MRR for this one-off exception. Any request to go below 65% requires CEO-level approval.
2) Opt-out mechanics: approve single opt-out trigger, 72-hour notice, max 90-day duration.
3) Billing: approve pro-rata billing by default; any credit > pro-rata (up to the 1-month cap) must be explicitly pre-approved by Revenue Ops.
4) Re-onboarding fee: approve the 10% re-onboarding fee.
5) Legal signoff mandatory: Legal must sign off on the amendment language and the SLA fallback path before DocuSign can be executed.

Karthik — please update the amendment doc and loop Legal. Aisha — proceed to preserve the DocuSign thread but mark as pending legal. If procurement pushes back hard on 60%, escalate to me immediately with the specific ask and proposed offset.

Vivek
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

On Wed, Sep 15, 2027 at 09:15 AM, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Noted — I'll get the updated amendment over to Legal this afternoon and include the fallback model variant wording.
>
> Karthik
